title: Shelf‑Stochastic KV Quantization Probe: progressive per‑layer shelves + reheating fallback
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: evaluate a new 'shelf‑stochastic' quantization strategy for KV caches that combines per‑layer small 'shelves' of quantized precision with a lightweight stochastic noise model to preserve rare high‑magnitude entries. The technique aims to reduce GPU memory footprint for long context workloads while limiting downstream quality regressions. We will compare against baseline uniform INT8/FP8 packing and our existing blockwise fallback approach.
hypothesis: A layer‑aware shelf quantizer (per‑layer variance bands with stochastic reheating for outliers) will achieve >=40% average KV memory reduction versus FP16 baseline for Llama2‑13B style caches with <=1.5% relative degradation in held‑out generation quality (token‑level KL and paired perplexity) and negligible impact on short‑latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Memory: median KV memory reduction >=40% on 8 representative prompt mixes; 2) Quality: average relative delta of token logprob and paired perplexity <=1.5% across eval sets; 3) Safety: no systematic failure modes on prefix continuation tests (>99.5% pass of continuity checks); 4) Runtime: add <2ms per request overhead in continuous batching path on A100-80GB profiling (p50).
test_plan:
- Phase A: offline simulation (float reference) on cached KV dumps from production traces (3M requests sample) to quantify quantization error maps per layer.
- Phase B: controlled online shadow traffic on dedicated A100 pool with 1% traffic, compare outputs vs production model using nll and reranking.
- Phase C: human eval sampling for representative prompt families where nll diverges.
Metrics: token logprob delta, paired perplexity, rerank AUC, end‑to‑end latency p50/p95, memory bytes per token, fallback rate.
progress_summary: Design completed (shelf widths and per‑layer variance estimator chosen). Implemented offline emulation harness and initial batch of quantizers. Ran Phase A simulations on 3 representative models (7B/13B/34B small variants). Observed promising memory savings but two outlier layers with heavy degradation on rare long‑token prefixes.
decisions:
- Use per‑layer shelf widths proportional to rolling standard deviation of KV activations instead of absolute magnitude bins.
- Integrate a stochastic reheating step: with probability p(layer,mag) we retain higher precision for entries exceeding a dynamic threshold.
- Fallback policy: on realtime inference, mark a request for reheating fallback if prefix continuity check triggers >3 token divergence.
- Rollout plan: Shadow -> Canary 5% -> Canary 25% with auto‑rollback on regression alarms.
implementation_notes: - Implemented emulation in Python to compute shelf-map and reheating probabilities.\n- Kernel integration planned as two parts: 1) quantized KV storage layout with per‑shelf headers; 2) reheating sampler that consults a small LRU bloom per GPU to track hot keys.\n- Will collaborate with runtime team to keep continuous batching path lock‑free when consulting reheating bloom.
risks_mitigation: Risks: (a) reheating sampler adds nontrivial CPU/GPU overhead; mitigation: keep reheating sampling probability low and use bitpacked bloom to avoid memory amplification. (b) Rare catastrophic regressions on specific prefixes; mitigation: targeted human eval and canary rollback. (c) Complexity in cross‑GPU shard handoffs; mitigation: keep shelf map deterministic and include versioned headers for compatibility.
next_steps: 1) Finish kernel layout prototype and microbench timing (due 2026-03-14). 2) Run Phase A extended sweep with 20M dumps (due 2026-03-20). 3) Prepare shadow rollout infra checklist with SLO gating (due 2026-03-24).
